title: Ordinary common-quotient tensor maps and quotient units
statement: Let $C$ be a site, $R,B$ commutative ring sheaves and $\varphi:R\to B$. Let $D$ be a common-quotient tower presentation [def-weil-pbc-common-quotient-tower-presentation]: $S_n$ is a tower with compatible locally surjective maps $q_n:R\to S_n$ and maps $b_n:B\to S_n$ such that $(\varphi,q_n,b_n,1)$ is a pushout. Write $I_n=\ker q_n$. Use the module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the ordinary sheafified scalar-extension functors $E^R_n,E^B_n$ in the cochain models [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. There is a natural $S_n$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(-)E^R_n\cong E^B_n$ carrying the canonical sheafification-unit image of $s\otimes m$ to that of $s\otimes m$. There are natural $R$-linear transitions $E^R_{n+1}\operatorname{Res}_{q_{n+1}}\to E^R_n\operatorname{Res}_{q_n}$ carrying $s\otimes x$ to $t_n(s)\otimes x$, and natural quotient units $\eta_n:1\to E^R_n\operatorname{Res}_{q_n}$ carrying $x$ to $1\otimes x$. The units commute with transitions. For every $R$-module sheaf $M$, $\eta_n(M)$ is epi and its sectionwise kernel is precisely local membership in the span of products $jx$, $j\in I_n$, as defined in the common-quotient presentation. No flatness hypothesis or complexes occur in this assertion.

proof.text: For a locally surjective q:R→S, form the sectionwise quotient presheaf R/ker(q) as an R-module presheaf. Its map to Res_q(S) is pointwise injective and locally surjective. Tensoring this map with M becomes an isomorphism after sheafification, hence the tensor map is locally injective. The underlying ordinary change-of-rings tensor is identified with this tensor by its explicit tensor comparison. If 1 tensor x vanishes after sheafification, local injectivity implies it vanishes locally in (R/I) tensor_R M. Mathlib quotTensorEquivQuotSMul sends 1 tensor x to [x], so x is locally in I M. The product I M is the span of products jx, j∈I. Conversely any R-linear map to an S-module kills these products; naturality and sheaf separatedness imply it kills local ideal products. This proves the full unit-kernel formula in Lean without assuming it in OrdinaryCommonQuotientTower.

proof.text: Prove unit epimorphy in Lean by induction on presheaf tensor sections. A pure scalar locally lifts along q, so s tensor x is locally 1 tensor (r x). Sums lift on the intersection covering sieve. Compose this locally surjective presheaf unit with the locally surjective sheafification unit, and reflect epimorphy from abelian sheaves. Transport along each ordinary model object equality.

proof.text: Form the pushout P of the underlying ring presheaves. Evaluation identifies P(U) with B(U) tensor_R(U) S(U). Sheafify P as a ring presheaf; the sheafification adjunction and the stipulated ring-sheaf pushout show that its induced map to S is an isomorphism. Thus the presheaf multiplication map P→S is locally injective. The tensor-ring identification proves that the module-presheaf multiplication B tensor_R Res_b(S)→Res_b(S) is locally injective, and 1 tensor s gives pointwise surjectivity. Sheafification makes this multiplication an isomorphism. Identify it with the ordinary adjunction counit on Res_b(S) using the unit formula at 1 tensor s. Apply the proved ordinary flat coefficient comparison, whose only hypothesis is invertibility of that counit. A standard-universe normalization supplies its auxiliary presentation. Finally the object and map equalities of the prescribed cochain models give natural isomorphisms to that presentation; cancelling these transports proves the required pure-section formula. No flatness assumption, sectionwise surjectivity, or choice of local lifts is used in this comparison.

proof.text: For q:R→S and t:S→T, use the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction for q. Transpose the explicit unit for q followed by t (more precisely the unit for q≫t), using the canonical composition isomorphism for restrictions, to construct a natural S-linear map E_q→E_(q≫t) Res_t. Restrict to R and compose with the restriction-composition isomorphism. The adjunction equation gives the formula on 1 tensor x. S-linearity and the identity η(s tensor x)=s·η(1 tensor x) give the formula on every pure tensor. Transport to the prescribed cochain models by their object and map equalities. Naturality of the tower projections identifies q_(n+1)≫t_n with q_n. Choosing these proved maps and the comparisons of step 3 constructs OrdinaryCommonQuotientTower. Its explicitly constructed units, epimorphy, kernel and compatibility remain as independently proved above.

proof.text: The section normalizations uniquely determine all retained data. Units agree sectionwise. Restrict a pair of comparison maps to R, and precompose with the epic quotient unit on the restricted B-module. Their formulas at 1 tensor x agree, hence the composites agree on all sections; cancel the unit. The restriction functor does not change underlying functions, so the original S-linear maps are equal. The same cancellation with the unit at level n+1 proves uniqueness of a transition. Proof irrelevance yields equality of the full OrdinaryCommonQuotientTower records. This is proved in Lean to verify uniqueness of the data chosen from the remaining existence theorem.

proof_origin.place: T5 extracted the underived quotient calculation (original item proof steps 2–3 and the underived part of step 5); sources as above. T5 proved quotient-unit epimorphy, the full local ideal-product kernel calculation via local tensor bijectivity and quotient tensors, and transition compatibility. The retained existence theorem supplies normalized ordinary maps only. Uniqueness of every retained map is also formally proved by cancellation of the epic quotient units. The quotient units and their naturality are explicit constructions; only the ordinary comparison and coefficient transitions remain in the existence statement. C3 completed the retained existence theorem: sheafified presheaf pushouts prove the multiplication counit invertible, the existing ordinary comparison gives the normalized isomorphism, and adjunction gives coefficient transitions. All auxiliary lemmas are proved privately in the same module; no new holes or nodes.
